newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer - stability, jobs not mutually exclusive.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer - stability, jobs not mutually exclusive.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday there has been growing recognition that monetary stability is indispensable for long-term growth which promotes employment and fosters social cohesion.

"Stability and employment are not mutually exclusive," Tietmeyer said in the text of a speech, adding that he was pleased the Amsterdam summit of European Union leaders on June 16 and 17 "seems to have realised this".
Tietmeyer added that the encouraging increase in price stability in Europe was also a result of preparations for European monetary union.
He predicted that the average rate of inflation in the European Union was likely to fall in 1997 from the 1996 rate of 2.5 percent.

"The financial markets react very sensitively these days to political and economic changes that herald risks of inflation. It is possible that higher interest rates and exchange rate reactions will then quickly follow," Tietmeyer said in the speech to the European Equity Traders Convention of the Federation of European Stock Exchanges in Frankfurt.
He added, "Internal stability is and remains the sole genuine seal of approval for a good currency."
A copy of the speech was made available ahead of delivery.
